text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing sporadic p95 spikes for short requests (<80 tokens) on staging. Traces point to routing choosing the fused-long kernel path for seqlen 32/48, which blows up tail latency.

jin: ugh. Is that the new sentinel-based routing change? any logs or perf dump?

maria: Yeah, looks related. Attached profiler snapshot (excerpt):
```
# kernel selection trace (simplified)
request id=0x7fa seqlen=48 -> chosen_path=fused-long-kernel v=2.1
kernel exec: 12.4ms (prefill) + 28.2ms (decode)
kv lookup: 0.6ms
batching delay: 6.9ms (waiting for batch)
end-to-end: 56.5ms p95
```

perf-bot: Automated stats from canary-run: p50=14ms p95=54ms p99=89ms for seqlen=48 decode workloads (1000 reqs) — baseline (pre-change) p95=18ms.

oz: Interesting — fused-long-kernel has better throughput for >256, but regresses on short contexts due to kernel prologue + larger shared mem setup. The autotuner probably saw a mixed seq distribution and picked long path to maximize token throughput.

noah: Can we change the picking heuristic to consider absolute per-request latency cost, not just throughput-per-batch? For example bias toward short-kernel if seqlen <= 64 AND measured batch size <= 8.

laura: Also seeing more KV cache churn when short requests get routed to long path; long path ends up touching larger KV blocks and evicting recently used small-context keys. I can reproduce with a simple workload that alternates seqlen 48 and 512.

maria: Repro script I used:
```bash
./tools/bench --model redwood-small --mode decode --seq-lens 48,512 --ratio 5:1 --concurrency 12 --profile > out.log
```
Out shows increased GPU memcpy overhead and KV evictions around iteration ~420.

jin: Proposal: 1) Add a latency-cost term to kernel score: score = throughput_score - alpha * est_per_request_latency. 2) Add hysteresis so that once a request shape is assigned to short-path, it stays there for N seconds unless metrics strongly favor switching.

oz: Proof-of-concept autotuner patch I ran locally:
```diff
- score = throughput_est(seqlen, batch)
+ score = throughput_est(seqlen, batch) - 0.8 * latency_penalty(seqlen)
```
Result: p95 for seqlen=48 dropped from 54ms -> 19ms, p50 unchanged. No impact on long (>256) median throughput in my small canary.

perf-bot: Canary run (after patch): seqlen=48 p95=20ms p99=44ms, seqlen=512 throughput delta -1.3% (within noise).

noah: Nice. We should also adjust KV cache alignment: short-path should use compact kv layout to avoid touching hot pages. Laura, can you add a small KV allocation policy for short-path?

laura: Yep — I'll add a flag to the allocator: --kv-layout=compact-for-short. Quick test shows ~30% fewer evictions for alternating workload.

maria: Action items:
- oz: open PR with autotuner score change + unit tests
- laura: add KV allocator flag and benchmark script
- jin: run a 24h canary in us-west1 with mixed workload 80% short/20% long and collect p50/p95/p99 and kv-eviction rates
- noah: add config knob in rollout: soft-fallback to short-path if p95>30ms for short requests

oz: I'll draft PR today. One more thought — we should expose the alpha (latency penalty weight) as a runtime-config so we can tune per-cluster.

jin: Agreed. Also add telemetry tags so the Console can filter by "autotuner-path" and "kv-layout".

maria: If everyone is okay, let's run the canary tonight at 11pm PT. I'll be online to roll back if needed. :white_check_mark:

noah: +1

laura: +1, already have the mini-benchmark ready.

perf-bot: Canary scheduled at 2026-03-17T07:00:00Z for cluster:staging-us-west1 (1000s mixed requests).

maria: thanks team — will post results in this thread after the run. :slightly_smiling_face:
